purpose: Translate dark-game lighting professional practice into actionable Ashwake repair gates.
principles: Darkness must be readable through value design, not blanket brightness.
Subject needs value separation from background through silhouette, rim edge, local contrast, and color-temperature split.
Midtones carry navigation and form; deepest blacks belong only in non-critical negative space.
Emissive materials may support mood, signage, and accents, but must not be the sole lighting system.
Exposure and tone mapping must protect material/form readability without crushing the toe or clipping emissive shoulders.
ashwake_repair_order: Define gameplay-critical regions of interest for start, first relic, safe window, hostile, success, failure.
Capture grayscale thumbnails plus Lumen Overview, Lumen Scene, Surface Cache, HDR Eye Adaptation where possible.
Lock or bound exposure during QA so auto exposure cannot hide lighting defects.
Assign subject/background value lanes and reserve deep black for non-critical negative space.
Add motivated sources: cold roof daylight, low forge bounce, gold seam pulses, rim/kicker from broken clerestory or furnace throat.
Inspect Lumen surface/cache behavior; support tiny important emissives with actual light actors or larger luminous geometry.
Tune tone mapping/grade after art lighting; do not use global brightness as repair.
Validate with emissive in/out of frame, bloom off/on, grayscale, thumbnail, and low-display-brightness screenshots.
known_failure_modes: global exposure compensation masquerading as lighting fix
histogram dominated by black spike and emissive spike
auto exposure adapts to edge emissive and darkens subject
no fill or bounce plane behind attractive silhouette
dark hero prop against dark wall with no rim
tiny bright emissive causing Lumen noise/flicker or missing GI
single giant room mesh with poor Lumen surface cache coverage
